Creates Solana shreds from entry batches, with FEC, Merkle proofs, and signatures.

# Purpose
This file implements the lifecycle and batch processing logic for `fd_shredder_t`, which is the object that converts an entry batch into Solana-style shreds. It defines the create, join, leave, and delete functions for managed memory use, and it validates memory alignment and object state with the `magic` field. The initialization code also stores the signer callback and signer context, then prepares the shredder state for later batch work.

The main function is [`fd_shredder_next_fec_set`](<#fd_shredder_next_fec_set>), which builds one forward error correction set from the current entry batch. It selects the shred type, computes data and parity shred counts, fills shred headers and payloads, adds Reed-Solomon parity data, computes Merkle tree leaves and proofs, signs the Merkle root, and writes the final signature and proof data into each shred. The file also tracks batch offsets and shred indexes across calls with [`fd_shredder_init_batch`](<#fd_shredder_init_batch>), [`fd_shredder_skip_batch`](<#fd_shredder_skip_batch>), and [`fd_shredder_fini_batch`](<#fd_shredder_fini_batch>), so the caller can process a batch in parts and keep the shred sequence consistent.
